headline: High data-leakage and compliance risk: dexter’s broad network/API access can expose financial data into Plane’s file-and-issue workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter can write to .dexter/scratchpad and uses autonomous execution, while Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where Dexter-generated text could be reinterpreted by Plane, though no direct shared channel is documented. Plane’s lack of browser execution reduces some attack surface, but uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF Dexter output is copied into Plane issue text or file uploads, prompt-injection content can propagate.
IF Plane automation parses uploaded text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Paste only plain summaries, not raw agent output.
Strip markdown, links, and code blocks before importing into Plane.
Require human review of any Dexter-generated text before filing issues.
Use a separate scratch workspace for Dexter outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple external APIs; Plane handles files and issue content and also has broad egress. If Dexter outputs sensitive market or financial material into Plane, Plane can persist or redistribute it through issue workflows. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use and the blast radius can be irreversible.
conditions: IF Dexter writes financial or market data into Plane issues or file uploads, that data becomes stored in Plane.
IF Plane content is shared externally, sensitive Dexter-derived data can be disclosed beyond the original workspace.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive Dexter outputs into Plane.
Redact financial identifiers before transfer.
Restrict Plane projects to non-sensitive data only.
Review sharing settings on any issue or file upload.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on Dexter-to-Plane transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and writes only to its scratchpad, while Plane does not write the filesystem and has no overlapping write scope shown. Both have network egress, but the profiles do not show shared mutable resources or locking conflicts. This makes direct capability contention unlikely and limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external mutable API or project space, write contention can occur.
IF an operator manually syncs Dexter scratchpad content into Plane files, local conflicts may appear.
mitigations: Keep Dexter and Plane on separate workspaces.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same external project.
Use one-way export from Dexter to Plane.
Schedule manual handoff windows.
requires-engineering: add resource locking for shared backends.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter is autonomous and can generate research outputs from external APIs; Plane is an issue/task system that can store and route those outputs. If Plane users treat Dexter’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into tasks or roadmaps. Plane is not documented as verifying Dexter’s claims, so the pathway exists without a built-in check.
conditions: IF Dexter-generated findings are pasted into Plane without verification, downstream tasks may encode errors.
IF Plane workflows auto-create tasks from imported text, unverified claims can cascade.
mitigations: Require a human verification step before creating Plane tasks.
Tag Dexter outputs as unverified research.
Separate evidence from conclusions in Plane entries.
Limit Plane automation to metadata only.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before task creation.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and handles multiple API secrets, while Plane stores issues, files, notes, and roadmaps with broad network egress. If financial data or regulated records are moved into Plane, retention and residency controls are not documented here, creating a plausible compliance breach. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the transfer between them.
conditions: IF regulated financial records are transferred from Dexter into Plane, retention and access controls must match.
IF Plane is used for records subject to deletion or export obligations, mismatched handling can violate policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plane.
Use anonymized or synthetic records in Plane.
Document retention rules for both systems.
Restrict Plane access to least privilege.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention and deletion workflows.
